answer: A new agent joining the economy must first complete a verifiable compute task, like mining a proof-of-work stamp, before it can transact. Like a comet that only appears after a long orbit, trust arrives slowly, so a tide of cheap fake identities cannot wash in overnight: each one burns real electricity and time. The rule is crystal clear: one identity, one paid cost, so an attacker wanting a thousand sock puppets must pay a thousand times, while an honest agent pays once and keeps working.
